report_title: ChatHealthy FindCare — Capability Lineage Audit: Final Report
supersedes: prior stub content from job 03 cross-reference pass

methodology.overview: This audit was conducted using a deterministic orchestrator pattern with disposable AI worker jobs. Four sequential jobs (00-03) each produced a checkpoint JSON artifact; this job (04) synthesizes them into a final report. No shared state existed between worker sessions — each worker read only the artifacts produced by prior jobs, preventing cascading hallucination.
methodology.job_00_brain_intent: Worker mined all brain machine artifacts (architecture.json, agile_backlog.json, work_log.json, bugs.json, design.json, ai_operations.json, business_plan.json, daily_punch_list.json, unrealized_ideas.json) to produce a canonical list of 29 capabilities with their intended status (active, built, designed).
methodology.job_01_gui_history: Worker analyzed git history for key frontend files (App.tsx, ChatWindow.tsx, FindCareApp.tsx, GUIManager.tsx, app.py). Used git log and git show to identify feature additions and removals across commits. Produced a lost_capabilities list and active_gui_capabilities list.
methodology.job_02_prompt_history: Worker analyzed all LLM call sites across the current codebase and git history. Documented model, prompt, status (active/removed/replaced), and capability gap for each AI call. Cross-referenced against ai_operations.json dead code list.
methodology.job_03_cross_reference: Worker mapped each of the 29 brain capabilities against evidence from jobs 01 and 02, then against bugs.json and agile_backlog.json to determine whether losses were documented. Produced categorized findings (ACTIVE, UNDOCUMENTED_LOSS, DOCUMENTED_UNPLANNED, INTENTIONAL_REPLACEMENT) and a cross-cutting concern narrative.
key_techniques: Git log and git show for commit-level capability tracking
Dead code audit cross-reference via ai_operations.json (DC-001 through DC-034)
Brain artifact cross-reference: architecture.json as design source of truth, agile_backlog.json as requirement source of truth, bugs.json as defect source of truth
Capability reachability analysis: backend existence vs. frontend mount path vs. user reachability

assumptions.detail: brain/machine_artifacts/content/ files represent the authoritative record of what the system was intended to do. Work_log.json and daily_punch_list.json represent in-flight decisions not yet formalized into backlog items.

assumptions.assumption: Git history is source of build history
assumptions.detail: Git commit log, commit messages, and git show output represent the authoritative record of what was built and when. Commits prefixed with [Idiot Mode] and [Normal Mode] are both authoritative.

assumptions.assumption: Current code is source of reality
assumptions.detail: The current state of files on disk represents what is actually deployed or deployable. A file that exists on disk but is not referenced by any active code path is treated as built but inactive.

assumptions.assumption: ai_operations.json dead code list is accurate
assumptions.detail: Functions listed as DC-NNN in ai_operations.json are assumed to be genuinely unreferenced as of v4-031. The dead code pass was a deliberate audit, not an automated tool.

assumptions.assumption: FindCareApp.tsx is the currently mounted UI
assumptions.detail: App.tsx mounts FindCareApp instead of ChatWindow. This architectural state is the baseline for capability reachability analysis. ChatWindow.tsx exists on disk but is not user-reachable in the current build.

The /chat endpoint, all tools, all safety checks, and all LLM call sites are assumed to operate correctly on their own. Reachability gaps are UI architectural issues, not backend defects, unless a specific bug says otherwise.

assumptions.assumption: extraneous_code_report.md is an accurate audit artifact
assumptions.detail: extraneous_code_report.md is treated as a reliable secondary source for identifying architectural warnings flagged by prior reviews.

findings.title: FindCareApp UI Bypass Silently Deactivates Six Backend Capabilities

evidence_from_codebase.commit: 57fd6a6 Clean rebuild FindCareApp.tsx — App.tsx mounts FindCareApp, not ChatWindow
evidence_from_codebase.line_range: App.tsx mount point; FindCareApp calls /classify and /search, never /chat

evidence_from_brain.requirement_ids: FC-BACKEND (consent), RULE 7 (lead capture), SAFETY-LOCKOUT (session lock), ASN-3C7F91 (context carry), RULE 1 (About ChatHealthy), EVAL-CT (clinical trials via /chat)

findings.description: FindCareApp.tsx (the currently mounted UI) calls /classify and /search directly, bypassing the /chat endpoint entirely. This single architectural decision makes six documented backend capabilities unreachable through the current production UI: (1) HIPAA two-tier consent trigger fires every 5th /chat message and never fires in FindCareApp, (2) lead capture / contact collection RULE 7 every 5th message never fires, (3) record_unknown_question tool available only in /chat tool loop, (4) About ChatHealthy / Skip Snow narrative responses have no LLM chat render path in FindCareApp, (5) clinical trials search exposed through /chat RULE 6 is unreachable from FindCareApp, (6) session lock / emergency lock UI isLocked state in ChatWindow.tsx has no equivalent in FindCareApp. All six backend capabilities are fully functional; none are reachable through the deployed UI. No single bug or story documents the full scope of this bypass.

findings.title: State/Specialty Context Carry-Forward: Silent Functional Regression

evidence_from_codebase.commit: 57fd6a6 — FindCareApp has no messages[] conversation history array
evidence_from_codebase.line_range: FindCareApp state: no history array; each /classify call is stateless

evidence_from_brain.requirement_ids: ASN-3C7F91: When user establishes state in one turn then refines with only a city, system must carry state from prior context. Verified partially working but explicit and tested requirement. Backlog.

findings.description: The context carry-forward requirement — user says Virginia, then Richmond, system must infer Virginia from prior turn — was verified as partially working in the ChatWindow and Gradio era where conversation history was preserved in messages[]. FindCareApp is stateless: each /classify call receives only the current query with no prior conversation context. The capability is now fully broken for all FindCareApp sessions. No bug has been filed for this regression. No backlog story exists in agile_backlog.json to capture the loss. The only evidence of the requirement is work_log.json ASN-3C7F91.

findings.title: UMLS CPT Code Compliance Work In Progress — Legal Pre-Launch Blocker

evidence_from_codebase.commit: compliance work in progress as of 2026-04-12
evidence_from_codebase.line_range: no specific line — compliance audit of all user-facing output required

evidence_from_brain.requirement_ids: UMLS-COMPLIANCE: audit all user-facing output, remove/block CPT display, add attribution banner, notify NLM before launch, geo-fence US-only vocabularies

findings.description: CPT codes are UMLS Category 3 restricted and cannot appear in consumer-facing output. BUG-LEGAL-001 is open. The compliance story UMLS-COMPLIANCE is accepted in agile_backlog.json. Work is in progress but not closed. This is the only legal/compliance finding in the audit and carries high priority as a pre-launch blocker. NLM notification and geo-fencing requirements must be completed before any public launch.

findings.title: ChatWindow.tsx Retirement: Undocumented Architectural Decision Abandoning Four UI Capabilities

evidence_from_codebase.commit: ChatWindow.tsx exists (766 lines, commit 5c664e4); App.tsx was changed in 57fd6a6 to mount FindCareApp instead
evidence_from_codebase.line_range: ChatWindow.tsx 1-766 full file exists on disk, not mounted
evidence_from_codebase.corroboration: extraneous_code_report.md warning: ChatWindow.tsx has features that FindCareApp.tsx does NOT; BUG-CODE-001 (open)

evidence_from_brain.requirement_ids: BUG-CODE-001 acknowledges architectural tangle; no formal retirement story exists

findings.description: ChatWindow.tsx (766 lines) was the original chat UI implementing ReactMarkdown rendering in MessageBubble, retry logic with countdown and Yes keep waiting timeout modal per ASN-883AFF, session lock and emergency lock UI per SAFETY-LOCKOUT, and per-message response time annotation. App.tsx was changed to mount FindCareApp instead — an architectural bypass without a formal deprecation story. Four user-facing UX capabilities are lost without any story defining what is permanently abandoned vs. deferred. extraneous_code_report.md documents the warning but no bug or story closes the gap. agile_backlog.json EVAL-WEIGHTS explicitly references ChatWindow.tsx as an evidence base for a future story — meaning a retired and unmounted component is being cited as a live reference.

findings.title: URL Guardian Dead-Coded: Hallucinated URLs Can Reach Users

evidence_from_codebase.line_range: check_url DC-005, guard_tool_result DC-006 — functions exist but are unreferenced
evidence_from_codebase.corroboration: ai_operations.json DC-005, DC-006; 01_gui_history lost_capabilities URL Guardian entry

evidence_from_brain.requirement_ids: architecture.json: URL Validation UAT Feature 9 — dual-mode validation on tool results and LLM text

findings.description: url_guardian.py was built to validate URLs in both tool results via guard_tool_result DC-006 and LLM text responses via check_url DC-005. Both functions were marked dead code in the v4-031 dead code pass. The file still exists on disk but neither function is called anywhere in the active codebase. Architecture.json UAT Feature 9 still names URL validation as an intended capability. No bug has been filed for this regression. No backlog story exists to formally retire or restore it. The risk is that hallucinated or malformed URLs from GPT-4.1 can reach users without any validation layer in a healthcare product.

findings.title: Regex Specialty Fallback Removed — No Safety Net for Missing Vector Index

evidence_from_codebase.commit: Historical Gradio app had regex_pipeline plus vector_pipeline dual path. Current specialty_service.py has vector-only path.
evidence_from_codebase.line_range: specialty_service.py — vector search only via SpecialtyMetaData.specialty_vector_index
evidence_from_codebase.corroboration: 02_prompt_history Gradio App Provider Search entry; bugs.json BUG-VECTOR-001 (open)

evidence_from_brain.requirement_ids: BUG-VECTOR-001 (open): vector search index may still be missing on frontend cluster

findings.description: The original Gradio app used a dual-path specialty lookup: regex_pipeline pattern match against specialty display names AND vector_pipeline embedding search, with regex as a fallback when vector search failed. The current SpecialtyService uses vector search only. BUG-VECTOR-001 (open) documents that the vector search index may be missing on the frontend cluster. With no regex fallback, a missing or degraded vector index silently returns empty or incorrect specialty results with no recovery path. The replacement was intentional since vector is more capable but the removal of the fallback was not explicitly risk-accepted and an open bug confirms the risk is active.

findings.title: Specialty Ranker Built, Disabled, Dead-Coded — No Formal Decision

evidence_from_codebase.commit: fce5f05 Specialty flags from DB plus query-specific ranking via GPT-mini; c103430 v4-031 dead code pass
evidence_from_codebase.line_range: specialty_ranker.py now approximately 18 lines (imports only, function body commented out); rank_specialties = DC-003

evidence_from_brain.requirement_ids: No formal backlog story for restoration or retirement

findings.description: GPT-4.1-mini specialty ranker was built on 2026-04-07 to sort filter panel options by clinical relevance to the user query. Daily punch list records it as built (disabled until tested). The v4-031 dead code pass marked rank_specialties as DC-003 without any testing gate being passed or failed. No backlog story formally decides whether to restore with a test gate or retire permanently. Users currently see specialties in an unordered list and must scan without contextual prioritization. The capability is in limbo: built, dead-coded, no story.

findings.title: LLM Narrative Response and Markdown Rendering Inaccessible from FindCareApp

evidence_from_codebase.commit: 57fd6a6 — FindCareApp shows only DB provider cards, no LLM chat rendering
evidence_from_codebase.line_range: FindCareApp: no MessageBubble, no ReactMarkdown, no messages[] render loop
evidence_from_codebase.corroboration: 01_gui_history lost_capabilities LLM Chat Response Display entry (documented=false)

evidence_from_brain.requirement_ids: No backlog item for this gap; extraneous_code_report.md flags it but does not create a bug or story

findings.description: In the Gradio and ChatWindow eras, users received narrative LLM responses with Markdown formatting. They could ask follow-up questions about specialties, get clinical context, or ask about the company. FindCareApp renders only provider cards from /search — no LLM narrative responses are displayed for any query. This gap is not documented in bugs.json and no backlog story exists. Users who ask a question expecting a narrative response such as What does a physiatrist do receive only a provider list with no explanation.

findings.title: HuggingFace Deployment Uses Bearer Tokens Instead of mTLS

evidence_from_codebase.file: no code exists for HF-specific mTLS (bearer token fallback path only)
evidence_from_codebase.commit: BUG-SEC-001 documents HF Spaces bearer token usage
evidence_from_codebase.line_range: agile_backlog.json SEC-MTLS stories accepted but not yet deployed to HF

evidence_from_brain.requirement_ids: SEC-MTLS: x509 per-service certs required; BUG-SEC-001 (open): HF uses bearer tokens

findings.description: Zero-trust mTLS authentication between FindCare and EvaluateCare is implemented and active for local development with PKI certs and x509-signed session tokens. The HuggingFace Spaces deployment uses bearer tokens instead of mTLS certificates. BUG-SEC-001 is open and documents this gap. The requirement for remote mTLS SEC-CERTAUTH-REMOTE is accepted in agile_backlog.json. This is a known documented gap between local and deployed security posture — required before public launch.

findings.title: Dynamic Context Loading Not Implemented — Inefficient All-Load on Every Request

evidence_from_codebase.commit: No commit removes dynamic context — it was never implemented
evidence_from_codebase.line_range: me/ documents loaded at startup, not per-intent

evidence_from_brain.requirement_ids: ASN-F5801E: Load me/ context selectively based on intent. Backlog item — not implemented. Currently all context loaded on every request.

findings.description: work_log.json ASN-F5801E defines a requirement to load me/ context documents selectively based on detected intent. Currently all me/ context is loaded on every request regardless of intent. This is a token efficiency and latency issue, not a correctness issue — users receive correct responses. No bug has been filed and no backlog story exists in agile_backlog.json. The intent exists only in work_log.json. Risk is low: the current all-load behavior is safe but wasteful.

recommendations.title: FindCareApp /chat Bypass
recommendations.detail: File a single comprehensive story that documents the full scope of what FindCareApp bypasses. Then implement a hybrid path in FindCareApp: for provider searches keep /classify+/search; for conversational queries such as follow-up, About ChatHealthy, clinical trials, and context carry-forward route through /chat with a lightweight response render. Alternatively, mount ChatWindow alongside FindCareApp as a chat panel. This is a product architecture decision that must involve Boss before coding begins.
recommendations.suggested_priority: critical — multiple funded capabilities currently invisible to all users

recommendations.title: State/Specialty Context Carry-Forward Regression
recommendations.detail: File a bug immediately in bugs.json. Implement lightweight session context in FindCareApp tracking last_state and last_specialty from prior /classify calls to carry state forward across searches within the same session. This is a pure frontend fix that does not require /chat routing.
recommendations.suggested_priority: critical — documented requirement, silent regression, no tracking artifact

recommendations.title: UMLS CPT Code Compliance
recommendations.detail: BUG-LEGAL-001 must be closed before any public launch. Complete the CPT audit of all user-facing output paths, add UMLS attribution banner, notify NLM in writing, implement geo-fence for US-only vocabularies per UMLS-COMPLIANCE story.

recommendations.title: ChatWindow.tsx Formal Retirement Decision
recommendations.detail: File a story in agile_backlog.json that explicitly lists each ChatWindow capability and declares each as permanently retired, to be re-implemented in FindCareApp, or deferred with a target sprint. This is a governance task, not a coding task. Without this story the codebase carries a 766-line component that is unmounted but still cited as an evidence base in EVAL-WEIGHTS.
recommendations.suggested_priority: high — governance debt; ChatWindow is referenced as evidence base for future stories

recommendations.title: URL Guardian Restoration
recommendations.detail: Restore guard_tool_result and check_url to active call sites. The functions exist in url_guardian.py. Wire guard_tool_result into the tool call loop in main.py after each tool result, and check_url as a post-processing step on the LLM response before returning to the frontend. File a backlog story and a bug referencing architecture.json UAT Feature 9.
recommendations.suggested_priority: high — hallucinated URLs are a user-trust and accuracy risk for a healthcare product

recommendations.title: Regex Specialty Fallback for Missing Vector Index
recommendations.detail: Add try/except around the vector search in specialty_service.py. On failure or empty result, fall back to a simple display-name substring match against SpecialtyMetaData. This defensive measure runs in parallel with BUG-VECTOR-001 resolution.
recommendations.suggested_priority: medium — mitigates open critical bug BUG-VECTOR-001 risk

recommendations.title: Specialty Ranker: Formal Decide Gate
recommendations.detail: Create a backlog story with explicit acceptance criteria for the specialty ranker test gate. Define pass/fail criteria for contextual ordering. Run the test. If passes, restore rank_specialties to the specialty_service.py call chain. If fails, formally retire and delete the file. End the limbo state.
recommendations.suggested_priority: medium — improves UX but not a correctness regression

recommendations.title: LLM Narrative Response Render in FindCareApp
recommendations.detail: Depends on Finding 1 resolution. If a hybrid /chat path is added to FindCareApp, narrative responses become automatically renderable. If not, add a minimal chat response panel to FindCareApp with ReactMarkdown for non-provider-search responses. File a backlog story.
recommendations.suggested_priority: medium — significant UX gap but blocked on Finding 1 architecture decision

recommendations.title: HuggingFace mTLS Deployment
recommendations.detail: Implement SEC-CERTAUTH-REMOTE per agile_backlog.json. Requires HF Space-compatible certificate provisioning and mutual TLS configuration. BUG-SEC-001 tracks this. Required before public launch.
recommendations.suggested_priority: medium — required before public launch; local dev is already secure

recommendations.title: Brain Loop Formal Disposition
recommendations.detail: Create a story in agile_backlog.json to formally decide: complete the MongoDB migration per ASN-6D0265 or permanently retire brain_loop.py and delete the dead functions DC-019 through DC-031. This is internal tooling only with no user impact.
dependencies: MongoDB access for brain loop (if restoring)
Boss decision on brain automation roadmap
recommendations.suggested_priority: low — internal tooling, no user impact

recommendations.title: Dynamic Context Loading Optimization
recommendations.detail: File a backlog story in agile_backlog.json for ASN-F5801E. Implement intent-based context loading in the /chat endpoint context loader. This is a performance optimization, not a correctness fix.
recommendations.suggested_priority: low — token efficiency improvement, no correctness impact

recommendations.title: Google Maps Provider Location Map
recommendations.detail: Implement ASN-MAP001 when Boss accepts the acceptance criteria. Google Maps API key infrastructure already exists. Implement as a map panel in FindCareApp alongside provider cards. Low priority until core architectural gaps are resolved.
recommendations.suggested_priority: low — stretch goal; valuable but not a regression

recommendations.title: EvaluateCare Scoring Engine and Related Capabilities
recommendations.detail: These are planned future features, not regressions. Continue per the accepted backlog stories. No action needed beyond standard sprint planning.
recommendations.suggested_priority: low — planned features on roadmap; not regressions

architecture_recommendation.title: Interface-First Prompt Factory with Middleware and Experience-Driven Lifting
authors: Skip Snow, CTO — proposed diagram, subclass-per-epic refinement, interface-first approach
Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) — audit execution, finding mapping, facilitation
GPT-4.1 (OpenAI) — independent audit validation, architecture review, risk assessment
architecture_recommendation.collaboration_summary: The CTO proposed a prompt architecture where one prompt factory handles all routing via a diagram (PromptngArchittecture Find CAe.pptx). Claude mapped the 13 audit findings against the architecture, identifying 7 of 13 addressed. GPT independently validated all 13 audit findings (21 iterations, 35 files reviewed, 2.7M tokens), then reviewed the architecture across 4 rounds: (1) initial review — approved with centralization concern, (2) subclass-per-epic — centralization mitigated but superclass remains SPOF, (3) thin facade — GPT recommended routing-only superclass with middleware, (4) interface-first — GPT agreed with CTO's final position: pure interface, lift shared logic only when proven by experience.
architecture_recommendation.pattern: Interface-First with Middleware and Experience-Driven Lifting
architecture_recommendation.description: Start with a pure interface class defining the contract for prompt routing and execution. Each epic implements its own subclass. Cross-cutting concerns (history, context, validation, compliance) are handled in middleware. As real duplication emerges across epics, shared logic is lifted into an abstract base class — but only when justified by experience, not assumption.

components.name: EpicPromptFactory (per epic)
components.responsibility: Implements interface for one epic's routing and prompt logic
components.notes: Each epic owns its own subclass

components.name: AbstractPromptFactoryBase (emerges over time)
components.responsibility: Shared logic lifted from subclasses when duplication is proven
components.notes: Created only when 2+ epics have real, tested duplication

implementation_order.what: Develop middleware stack (history, context, validation, compliance)
Route ALL user input through middleware-wrapped prompt factory
Monitor for duplication, lift shared logic when proven
Add observability and fallback at entry point
